gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-13 three of its named stations cannot ship this week from the maker: the PECRON F3000LFP (its top pick) is pre-order shipping early December, the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus is sold out, and the ALLPOWERS R4000 is sold out. The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra (3,072 Wh, 3,600 W, 7,200 W surge, $1,299) and the BLUETTI Elite 300 (3,014 Wh, $1,199) are in stock and clear ChatGPT's own 2,824 Wh bar for 12 hours at 25 % duty.
standout_why: I compared against runtimefit.com (cited; its PECRON price is dated Oct 17 and its other prices have no date or stock status), outagereadyhq.com (cited; it has the DELTA 3 Ultra at $1,349 and sold out as of Oct 22, which is stale, and has no PECRON, R4000 or Elite 300) and homebatteryreport.com (cited; it gives no prices). None of them gives today's stock status. ChatGPT's own answer recommends the PECRON at $899 without saying it is a pre-order. I could not read testedwatts.com (cited) because of an SSL certificate error.
decides: It changes the pick. For a 1/3 HP pump through a 12-hour outage you can buy now, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra at $1,299 is the in-stock station with a published 7,200 W surge and enough capacity: 3,072 Wh × 0.85 / (800 W × 25 %) = 13.1 h. The BLUETTI Elite 300 ($1,199, 12.8 h on the same arithmetic) is cheaper but I could not source a motor-start surge figure for it. The PECRON F3000LFP is cheaper still at $899 but does not ship until early December. For a literal 13 HP pump (13 × 745.7 W ≈ 9,694 W shaft power), the continuous rating of every unit priced here is too low; the highest is the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus at 7,200 W.
